paragraphs: Okay, friend, deep breath. That was a heavy one, and it's heavy on purpose, because God wants His people to see how serious it is to walk away from Him. The two sisters were His, and God says, "They became Mine" (Ezekiel 23:4). Then they went chasing other lovers anyway, and Oholah's lovers were the ones who turned on her (Ezekiel 23:9), while God says He will stir up Oholibah's lovers against her (Ezekiel 23:22).

Here's the part that gets me: Oholibah saw what happened to her sister Oholah and kept going anyway, and God says she "was more depraved than her sister" (Ezekiel 23:11). Shrugging off a warning is something people do all the time. I once smelled smoke coming off a cookie tray and said, "I'm sure it's fine," and it was never fine, friend. God says what was behind it all: "you have forgotten Me and have cast Me behind your back" (Ezekiel 23:35).

So what does that mean for you? Whatever you lean on in place of God will not hold you up. God's word is a fair warning, and fair warnings are a kindness, so keep God in front of you instead of behind your back. And stay close, baker, because this word about the two sisters isn't finished yet.
